def factor_intraday_calmness_stress_attenuated(df):
    """Intraday calmness via rolling mean cosine of intraday angle, attenuated by overnight downside stress."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    overnight_ret, intraday_ret = alpha_tools.decompose_overnight_intraday(df_copy["close"], df_copy["open"])
    theta = np.arctan(intraday_ret * 10)
    window = 20
    calmness = np.cos(theta).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    overnight_stress = overnight_ret.clip(upper=0.0).abs().rolling(window, min_periods=5).sum()
    stress_weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + overnight_stress * 10.0)
    factor = calmness * stress_weight
    factor.name = "factor_intraday_calmness_stress_attenuated"
    return factor
description: Rolling mean of cos(arctan(intraday_ret*10)) equals 1/sqrt(1+100*intraday_ret^2), a positive measure of intraday return stability inversely related to return magnitude. Multiplying by an overnight downside stress attenuation term (inverse of 1 + 10*rolling_sum of negative overnight returns) produces a factor that favors stocks with calm intraday dynamics and low overnight tail risk. This is a low-risk/quality style mechanism expected to retain residual cross-sectional predictive power after industry and size neutralization.
